summary: The candidate captures nearly all of the paper's internal mathematical infrastructure and principal results, including the parameterized-triple module, boundary algebra, evaluation lemma, Khovanov test lemma, gluing theorem, and all three handle-attachment formulas. Most statements are recognizable and mathematically useful, with generally accurate page locators. It is not flawless because the displayed gluing theorem repeatedly omits the essential base algebra from the tensor product, several conditions and local-unit details are compressed away, one duplicate of Lemma 3.9 has an incorrect direct-sum index, and external attribution is inconsistent. Overlapping extraction chunks also create substantial duplication, including repeated handle formulas and nearly identical 2- and 3-handle definitions.
strengths: All four central internal results are represented: the general gluing isomorphism and the 1-, 2-, and 3-handle attachment formulas.
The parameterized-triple skein module, the associated 3-manifold algebra, and the gluing map Psi are extracted as distinct definitions with substantially correct mathematical content.
The evaluation-induced algebra/module lemma and the Khovanov tangle test lemma are captured with their main isomorphisms and appropriate lemma classification.
The candidate preserves useful supporting infrastructure, including the inverse gluing construction, the 1-handle boundary actions, and the 2- and 3-handle subalgebra/module data.
Most locators agree with the relevant source pages, and explicit labels such as Lemma 3.9 and Theorem 4.1 are preserved.
issues: The Theorem 4.1 entries write an unbased tensor product instead of the required tensor product over the boundary algebra S^star(Y;P); only the separate Psi definition contains the essential subscript.
The foundational definition of the admissible functorial link homology theory is missing as an entry.
The external MWW skein-lasagna construction and Khovanov tangle-functor result are not independently and adequately extracted; the latter is replaced by a narrower gl_2/Khovanov comparison entry.
The Ren-Willis antecedent gluing surjection is represented as an internal definition without its literature attribution, so its provenance and classification are inaccurate.

External attribution is unreliable: the paper's own 2-handle formula is duplicated as an external proposition merely because its proof follows an earlier argument, and a 3-handle specialization of the paper's own Theorem 4.1 is also marked external.
One duplicate of Lemma 3.9 incorrectly indexes the second direct sum by b in H^n rather than b in B^n.
The triple-module definition compresses or drops precise boundary data, and the 3-manifold algebra entry omits its cylinder local units.

The raw pool contains extensive overlap duplication: the Khovanov lemma, gluing theorem, handle formulas, 2-handle subalgebra/submodules, and 3-handle structures appear more than once, sometimes with conflicting precision or classification.
Some detailed handle entries use inconsistent notation, including V versus Y for the acting algebra and X'_1 in a 3-handle relation where X_1 is intended.

entryLevelComparison.comment: The source assumptions appear in the embedded source text but were not promoted to a mathematical entry.
The direct-sum construction is correct, but some precise boundary and intersection conditions are compressed.
The algebra and multiplication are captured, but the local units supplied by cylinders are omitted.
The based tensor product, target, and compatible-boundary versus zero rule are represented.
No standalone externally attributed entry captures the foundational MWW construction.
Correctly marked external, but stated only in the B4 link case rather than covering the broader algebra/module role used by the paper.
The candidate captures a related comparison but not Khovanov's full bimodule-chain-complex tangle invariant.
The surjection is present, but it is classified as a definition and lacks the required external attribution.
Both the algebra isomorphism and associated module isomorphism are faithfully represented.
The first version is accurate; the duplicate version contains the erroneous index b in H^n.
The core isomorphism and label are captured, but both theorem statements omit the base algebra under the tensor product.
The concise entry states the Hochschild-homology result correctly; the later entry supplies a compatible quotient presentation.
The cabling quotient is covered, but the redundant external proposition misclassifies the paper's own result.
The quotient formula is captured, though duplicated with inconsistent acting-algebra notation and an incorrect external flag.
